legend: You are playing an online game, you have a team of N%%ZSMJ0%% players, and you decided to challenge your friend's team that also consists of N%%ZSMJ1%% players, let's call them team A%%ZSMJ2%% and team B%%ZSMJ3%% respectively. Each player has a specific strength, more specifically the ith%%ZSMJ4%% player in team A%%ZSMJ5%% has strength equal to i%%ZSMJ6%% for each i%%ZSMJ7%% between 1%%ZSMJ8%% and N%%ZSMJ9%%, and the jth%%ZSMJ10%% player from team B%%ZSMJ11%% has strength equal to j+1%%ZSMJ12%% for each j%%ZSMJ13%% between 1%%ZSMJ14%% and N%%ZSMJ15%%.

The total strength of a team is the product of strengths of all players in the team. To make the game fair, you can swap the ith%%ZSMJ16%% player from team A%%ZSMJ17%% with the ith%%ZSMJ18%% player from team B%%ZSMJ19%% for any i%%ZSMJ20%% between 1%%ZSMJ21%% and N%%ZSMJ22%%, in other words, you can only swap players that have the same index in both teams. You can repeat the previous operation any number of times.
A game is fair when both of the teams have a equal strengths. Can you make the game fair?
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases T%%ZSMJ23%% (1≤T≤105%%ZSMJ24%%). Description of the test cases follows.
Each of the following T%%ZSMJ25%% lines, contains a single integer N%%ZSMJ26%% (1≤N≤105%%ZSMJ27%%).
output: For each test case, if you can make the game fair then print in one line an integer M%%ZSMJ28%%,the total number of operations needed, on the next line print M%%ZSMJ29%% (1≤M≤N%%ZSMJ30%%) distinct integers, the indices where you want to apply the swap operation. If you can't make the game fair, then print in one line the value −1%%ZSMJ31%%.
Note that you don't have to minimize the total number of operations. If there exists more than one answer print any of them.
note: In the first test case, the initial strengths are:
team A%%ZSMJ32%%: 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8%%ZSMJ33%% with total team strength equal to 40320%%ZSMJ34%%.
team B%%ZSMJ35%%: 2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9%%ZSMJ36%% with total team strength equal to 362880%%ZSMJ37%%.
After swapping the players in indices 1,4%%ZSMJ38%% and 5%%ZSMJ39%%, the strengths become like this:
team A%%ZSMJ40%%: 2,2,3,5,6,6,7,8%%ZSMJ41%% with total team strength equal to 120960%%ZSMJ42%%.
team B%%ZSMJ43%%: 1,3,4,4,5,7,8,9%%ZSMJ44%% with total team strength equal to 120960%%ZSMJ45%%.
So the strengths are now equal and the game is fair.
In the second test case, you can't make the strengths equal no matter how you perform the swaps.
